registry.label: Textured full art
registry.years: BW textured promos, modern chase tiers
registry.note: Embossed rather than marked. This paper prints no dots, stars or lines, so its texture is a NORMAL MAP — the BW/XY deep relief — and not a mark sheet: the mark layer stays plain and the relief supplies the structure, which is why the registry points at a surface file.

photographs.question: Does any real photograph of BW43, BW73 or BW74 show the embossed lattice, and what does it settle?
photographs.method: band-passed luminance (blur 1.5 - blur 10), gradient-direction histogram and structure tensor per patch, autocorrelation of the profile across the dominant direction; the same photograph's card BACK is the control

thresholds.settlesEmboss: a front patch with r >= 0.25 and diagonal >= 0.35, not matched by the back

rakingLightSearch.outcome: No raking-light photograph yields a pitch this build will attribute to the emboss, so the relief keeps its modelled pitch and direction. One video was found and measured (verdict.video) and the Japanese listings do show the weave (verdict.weaveVisible): both are facts about the paper, and neither is a measurement of its ridges.

weaveVisible.where: three Japanese listings of プラズマ団ギフトセット 005/016 (BW73 in Japanese), four frames, all shot tilted under a point light
weaveVisible.what: a fine diagonal lattice of ridges over the whole printed face, the weave the front-lit slab photographs could not show
weaveVisible.whyItIsNotAPitch: the estimator returns a periodic peak on a SMOOTH card too: the BW75 control reads 6.68% of card width on the achromatic band against 4.37% for the four textured photographs, so a period here cannot be attributed to the emboss
weaveVisible.consequence: the relief keeps its modelled pitch, but the record now says the paper IS visible in oblique photographs, which is what the full-art mask describes

video.source: dFI0NbvBygY — "3 Full Art Promo Pokemon Cards (BCBM)", the English BW73 flat on a desk under one lamp
video.whyItIsNotAPitch: the same card's own flat catalogue scan reads 8.58% on the same band against 4.19% here, and the smooth control reads 6.68%; an estimator that returns 4% and 8% for one card is not tracking one stable property
video.atThisResolution: 720p — the patch crops are soft enough that the ridges blur into the artwork, while the 900–1200 px Japanese stills with a raking light do show them

highResolutionSweep.result: nothing sharper than what is already measured
highResolutionSweep.detail: no BW73 upload above 720p came back from ten 4K/close-up queries; the only 1080p master of a Team Plasma opening shows the card hand-held at about 350 px behind a sleeve, and the 4K holo showcases cover modern sets

verdict.statement: The photographs do NOT resolve the emboss: no front patch shows a repeat that its own card back does not, so the ridge geometry stays modelled.
verdict.settles: The LAYOUT, and that the weave is really there. All three are full-art printings whose illustration runs under the text wash (BW73 in both seller photographs, BW43 and BW74 in the catalogue scans), which is why the rows now use the full-art mask rather than a 37.5%-tall illustration window; and the oblique Japanese photographs show the lattice across that whole face, at a zoom where nothing else could be mistaken for it.
verdict.doesNotSettle: The ridge pitch, depth and direction. The oblique photographs show the weave but the same estimator reads a comparable period on a smooth card, so attributing the number to the emboss would be a choice dressed as a measurement. A front-lit phone photograph does not show the ridges at all, and no raking-light photograph or video of BW43, BW73 or BW74 was found.

cards.name: Landorus
cards.evidence: BW Black Star Promos: a textured full-art foil. One treatment per card from Pokumon’s holofoil taxonomy, corroborated where Bulbapedia tags the same variant printing. Pokumon does not date the retro-to-HD Cosmos switch per card, so every Cosmos claim here uses the retro sheet the programme opened on.
